content.comment_body: It would be helpful if the tool could allow reading inputs from an Excel spreadsheet. I'm programming [product_name] for tasks that depend on specific inputs, and simulating and testing is currently quite challenging. If the access tool could read directly from a spreadsheet, it would simplify simulation of analog inputs, letting me change values, adjust rate of change, and record outputs efficiently. Regards, [user_name]
Currently, the Access Tool does not support this functionality.
I realize it's not possible now – my intention was to suggest this as a valuable feature for future enhancements.
Why is this needed? If you want to test value changes from your PC, you can use the integrated webserver for such purposes.

I'm using [product_name] to monitor the rate of change for an analog input. It tells me when the input shifts by more than a set number of counts in a specific time frame. Simulating this accurately is challenging and labor-intensive. If [product_name] could read directly from a spreadsheet, it would make scenario setup easy and allow me to adjust inputs precisely and review results line-by-line. This would enable tiny, repeatable input changes and improve output recording.

Of course, it would be ideal to have an all-in-one tool with every function available and for a low cost. [company_name] enables many possibilities with the controller. If you set up an S7 or Modbus client on your PC, you can simulate scenarios as needed, treating the controller as the server. There are multiple client downloads available, even some for Excel. However, keep in mind packet-oriented connections are not real-time systems, which affects tracking accuracy. Developing features for extremely specialized use cases is often not economically feasible. Personally, I use a tool like Profilab for machinery protocols and prefer Modbus. If you know Visual Basic, you can develop your own Excel spreadsheets to work with S7 or Modbus and create custom utilities. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking an enhancement for the [product_name] Access Tool: the capability to import analog input data from Excel spreadsheets to streamline the simulation and testing process in [product_name] programming. The current workflow is seen as cumbersome, and importing test data would make it more accurate and efficient. While this feature is not currently available, suggestions include workarounds using existing protocols or third-party software. The conversation identifies this request as specialized and possibly not cost-effective for [company_name], yet it reveals the need for improved simulation and testing options for advanced users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] Access Tool to support importing or reading input values directly from Excel, making it easier to customize, simulate, and record input/output scenarios for their applications.
